sources.entry: Configs - Configuration file manager for quickly viewing, editing and managing config files. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/iHongRen/configEditor) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Configs is a macOS app, written in SwiftUI, for viewing, editing and managing dotfiles and other configuration files such as .zshrc and .gitconfig.
summary.what_it_does: Configs scans a Mac for common configuration files such as .zshrc, .bashrc, .gitconfig and .vimrc, and lets users add more by importing files individually or in batches or by dragging them into the window. It provides a code editor with syntax highlighting for several file types, plus search, zoom, dark mode and line numbers. Each edit is recorded automatically through Git, so users can view history, compare differences and restore a previous version. When a shell config like .zshrc is saved, the app runs source so changes take effect immediately. Files can be organized into custom groups and marked with short coloured tags, and the right-click menu opens files in Finder, Terminal, VSCode and similar apps. The interface is available in Chinese and English, following the system language by default with a manual switch in the About page.
use_cases: track history of config file changes
compare and restore earlier versions of a config
quickly open config files in an editor or terminal
tag config files with short labels
how_to_run: git clone (repository URL not filled in the README)
Open Configs.xcodeproj in Xcode, select 'My Mac' as the target, then Build (Cmd+B)
Or download Configs.dmg from the Releases page, drag Configs.app to /Applications
Open Configs.app from Applications or Launchpad
notable: Git-backed automatic version history with diff view and one-click restore
Runs source automatically after saving shell config files so edits apply immediately
Scans for common config files automatically and supports drag-and-drop import
Bilingual interface (Chinese and English) that follows the system language
caveats: Installing the prebuilt app requires running an xattr command to remove the quarantine flag, since the app is not signed for direct install
